author: roundtrip-audit
body:
# Independent integration audit (read-only)

Scope reviewed: shared lambda printer, new instance roundtrip regression, both helper call sites and empty-context guards, `_source_goal_helpers.py` composition, implementation digest inclusion, and Python direct consumers including scoped profile/transport validation.

## Actionable resource-limit asymmetry

`src/ladon/lean/ladon_scoped_slice_helper.lean:85-88` rejects printed target/proof strings above 1 MiB before parsing and elaboration. The analogous unscoped `checkedRoundtrip` in `src/ladon/lean/ladon_proof_slice_helper.lean:58-65` parses both strings first and has no corresponding text-size check; its structural serialization ceiling is checked later (around lines 153 onward). Thus a large closed proof/type can incur parser/elaborator work before the 1 MiB structural limit rejects it. This is pre-existing in unscoped logic but became a direct consumer of the shared printer; recommend matching the scoped pre-parse byte cap. No runtime repro run because assignment says no tests/builds.

## Checks with no finding

- The shared printer handles consecutive lambda binders, recurses through each binder body, preserves default/implicit/strict-implicit/instance binder syntax, avoids generated binder-name collisions, delegates non-lambda bodies to Lean's regular delaborator, and fails closed above depth 64. It does not change the expression graph or fvar identities.
- Both helpers still run roundtrip inside empty LCtx with anonymous namespace/no opens, prohibit postponement and errors-to-sorry, instantiate then reject expr/level metavariables, and independently check defeq against original target/proof.
- Scoped reconstruction continues substituting exact old fvars in context order, checking transported let values/application type, and checking closure. Provider observations remain in ordered proposition-argument sequence, and profile consumers accept the existing `scoped-identity-transport-v2` contract.
- Composition marker is unique-checked; shared file is packaged from `ladon/lean`; helper digest covers composed bytes and correspondence implementation digest now covers the shared printer.
- The new test covers scoped/unscoped x selected/used, retained instance binder rows, dependent local presence, complete extraction and source immutability. I did not execute it per assignment.

Coverage limitation: these checks and root's cited extraction establish complete extraction for the captured example, not provider replay or mathematical closure; the four provider-unreplayed frontiers and boundary remain as root reported.

author: roundtrip-audit
body:
# Follow-up audit addendum

Reviewed final unscoped helper and `tests/test_proof_slice_roundtrip_limits.py` read-only. The reported asymmetry is resolved: unscoped `checkedRoundtrip` now obtains proof text through the shared printer and rejects target/proof UTF-8 text above 1 MiB before either parser call, matching the scoped helper's ordering. The regression parameterizes both helpers, constructs an oversized closed target, and requires the limit error without timeout, memory, or output stop. It also preserves the same rejection text.

I found no weakening of the empty-LCtx/anonymous-namespace setup, disabled postponement/errors-to-sorry, metavariable rejection, or independent target/proof defeq checks. The helper change adds no consumer contract/profile changes. I did not run tests/builds, per assignment; root owns final suite and byte-identity verification.
